rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a concrete letter template: both letters invoke aviation's national importance, direct the Air Coordinating Committee through its chairman to develop work on the stated subject, and require coordination or consultation with the aviation industry and other interested groups. C02 is also materially similar in its aviation-policy review and consultation machinery, but it assigns the work to a specially created commission and is substantially more elaborate. C03 parallels the rationale for comprehensively reviewing a dynamic national policy field, though its operative structure and language are less closely matched.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The increasing importance of aviation as an instrument of national policy and to our national welfare
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The importance of aviation to our nation and to the world
shared_material.explanation: Both open the assignment by emphasizing aviation's broad national importance.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I therefore request that you, as Chairman of the Air Coordinating Committee, direct it to undertake a comprehensive review
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accordingly, I direct the Air Coordinating Committee to develop and coordinate plans
shared_material.explanation: Both use a presidential letter to the Committee's chairman to assign a defined aviation-related project to the same interagency body.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This should be done in consultation with appropriate industry, local government and private aviation groups.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is therefore appropriate that the Committee coordinate them with representatives of the aviation industry and other interested groups.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive shared consultation clause involving the aviation industry and other outside stakeholders.
